articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Países Bajos y Alemania en el Johan Cruyff Arena correspondiente a la jornada 1 del Grupo 2 de la Nations League
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Países Bajos y Alemania en el Johan Cruyff Arena correspondiente a la jornada 1 del Grupo 2 de la Nations League
articles.body: Países Bajos inicia una nueva etapa con Xavi Hernández al frente de la selección después de un último Mundial que terminó antes de lo esperado. El combinado neerlandés fue eliminado en dieciseisavos de final por Marruecos y afronta ahora una nueva edición de la Nations League con el objetivo de ir germinando un nuevo ciclo. El Johan Cruyff Arena será el escenario de un estreno de máxima exigencia, ya que enfrente estará una Alemania que también llega con nuevo proyecto. Favorito para el partido entre Países Bajos y Alemania Alemania afronta igualmente un cambio de ciclo con Jürgen Klopp al frente después del batacazo sufrido en el pasado Mundial. El conjunto germano también cayó en los dieciseisavos de final ante Paraguay en la tanda de penaltis y tratará de dejar atrás aquella decepción con un buen comienzo en la Nations League. El duelo se presenta como uno de los grandes atractivos de la primera jornada y las casas de apuestas reflejan la igualdad entre dos selecciones que buscan iniciar con victoria sus respectivos proyectos. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción especialmente interesante para las apuestas deportivas, teniendo en cuenta la contundente tendencia de ambos conjuntos. Países Bajos ha cumplido este pronóstico en sus cinco últimos partidos, mientras que Alemania también ha visto marcar a los dos equipos en cada uno de sus cinco encuentros más recientes. Los precedentes inmediatos apuntan, por tanto, hacia un encuentro con ocasiones en ambas porterías. Especialmente, entre dos selecciones que afrontan una nueva etapa y que buscarán empezar la Nations League con una victoria. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.43 por el 'sí' y de 2.66 por el 'no'. Gol en ambas mitades La tendencia de los dos combinados nacionales también invita a buscar goles repartidos durante los 90 minutos. En tres de los cinco últimos partidos de Países Bajos se ha marcado al menos un gol en cada una de las dos partes. Una estadística que asciende hasta el pleno en el caso de Alemania: sus cinco encuentros más recientes han tenido goles tanto en la primera como en la segunda mitad. 1XBET paga a 1.48 que haya gol en ambas partes y a 2.46 que no se produzca este escenario. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El historial más reciente de ambos equipos refuerza la posibilidad de un partido con varios goles. En cuatro de los cinco últimos encuentros de Países Bajos se han superado los 2.5 tantos totales. Exactamente, el mismo registro que presenta Alemania en sus cinco compromisos más recientes. La coincidencia de ambas tendencias convierte la línea de goles en otro mercado a tener en cuenta para un duelo entre dos selecciones que llegan al estreno de la Nations League con nuevos proyectos.

articles.title: Arizona State hockey coach declines repeatedly to talk about workout that left Matthew Mayich in a coma
articles.summary: Matthew Mayich collapsed during a team workout last month with the Sun Devils, and has been in a coma ever since.
articles.body:
Arizona State men's hockey coach Greg Powers did not want to talk Wednesday about the workout that left sophomore Matthew Mayich on life support .

Speaking for the first time publicly since Mayich was hospitalized more than a month ago, Powers insisted Arizona State is still "a great place to be" while refusing to address the incident repeatedly when speaking with reporters during the National Collegiate Hockey Conference's media day.

Mayich was participating in a workout with the team on Aug. 20 when he collapsed and later fell into a coma. He was taken to a local hospital, and has since been transferred to a neurological institute where he remains in a coma. The workout was described as "grueling" and run by an ex-Green Beret. Mayich allegedly showed obvious signs of distress and was unable to complete tasks throughout the workout.

Powers said Wednesday that it has been "a difficult time" for the Sun Devils' program, and that Mayich had been in "our thoughts and prayers."

"I know there will be more questions about Matthew, and we won't be able to answer those today," Powers said, via The Athletic .

Reporters pressed Powers repeatedly, and things got a bit heated at the virtual video conference. One reporter asked if Powers held himself responsible.

"Respectfully, I decline to answer any questions regarding Aug. 20," he replied, via The Athletic.

The reporter continued later and asked about the report that Arizona State released on Tuesday, which said Powers and his staff didn't submit the training activities to the school's strength and conditioning coaches for review. The report did not assign any blame for the incident.

NCHC associate commissioner Michael Weisman then jumped in.

"We said we're not here to talk about the report," Weisman said. "We said that at the beginning. We're here to talk about the season."

Later, a reporter asked Powers if any of his players had raised concerns before the workout. He declined to answer again. Powers was asked why he felt it was more important to talk about hockey rather than Mayich.

"Again, just not able to answer questions regarding it in any way," he replied.

The only real answer he gave regarding the subject came when he was asked how he would assure nervous parents about sending players to play for the Sun Devils after this incident.

"Everything that we believe — and so many players that have played here before and the guys that are here now — that is great about playing hockey at Arizona State still are great about playing hockey at Arizona State," Powers said. "We have an unbelievable university with, obviously, the opportunity to gain an incredible education. A vibrant market, a beautiful campus, a beautiful arena, with people and support here that are here for our student-athletes. Everything that has been great about coming here to play hockey still is."

Mayich was selected by the St. Louis Blues in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL Draft, and he transferred into Arizona State from Clarkson University (N.Y.) this past summer. He previously played in the Ontario Hockey League. His lawyer said earlier this month that he has "zero chance of recovery."

How Powers has modeled accountability for his team since the incident isn't something he wanted to get into, either.

Powers has led the Sun Devils for nearly two decades now. He played goalie for the program in the late 1990s, and led the team from the club level to an NCAA Division I program in 2015. He signed a five-year extension with the university last November.

The team finished last in the NCHC last season, and lost 10 of its final 12 games. The Athletic reported that he disparaged players last season using vulgar language, and called them while posting images in the locker room that included a picture of Charmin Ultra Soft toilet paper.

"In almost 20 years of doing this at this institution, I know there are a lot of people and young men that have really positive things to say about their experience here and the relationship we have that extends far beyond hockey," Powers said. "There are some things that have been said, and I respect anything anybody has to say. I believe that I am the right guy."

articles.title: Can Padres Offense Continue Their Hot Streak Into October?
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres are the hottest team in baseball. Despite their loss in the series opener against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Tuesday night, the Friars h...
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres are the hottest team in baseball . Despite their loss in the series opener against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Tuesday night, the Friars have still won 12 of their last 14 games in what has been an incredible stretch of baseball. Much, if not all, of that is due to the Padres offense. Prior to their game against the Dodgers, San Diego was averaging an insane 7.3 runs per game in their previous 11 games (since September 9).

Entering play on Wednesday, the Friars are now tied with the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies for the top NL Wild Card spot . The main question, however, is whether or not the Padres can continue to produce into October.

Can Padres Offense Continue Their Hot Streak Into October?

Back in 2024, the Padres seemed to be the team to beat. It may not have felt that way for much of the regular season, but they went on a tear in the second half. San Diego reeled off a ludicrous 16 wins in their final 24 games to clinch a playoff berth and secure consecutive 90-win seasons for the first time in franchise history. The Friars immediately swept the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card round with two commanding wins before turning to face Los Angeles in the NLDS.

The Dodgers got off to a good start, tagging starter Dylan Cease for five runs to win Game One. But the Padres immediately answered back, winning the next two games and putting L.A. on the ropes. They played Game Four in Petco Park, and San Diego had the edge. They needed just one more win. But they couldn't do it. Not only that, but the Friars failed to score for 24 consecutive innings. It was a pitiful showing from the offense, with the club falling 2-0 in the final game.

It was a similar story in 2025, with San Diego playing the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Neither team scored more than three runs in the series, and no more than four combined runs were scored in all three games. The Padres offense simply failed them in both events. That question permeates the discussion of any possible success this October.

One of the few things that's different about this Padres offense is their lineup being much more sturdy. The offense, top to bottom, looks steadier in a way that it has not in years past. During their playoff series in 2024 and '25, the Friars got virtually no production from the bottom of their lineup. San Diego has new contributors this season that help fill out that area in a big way.

For one thing, Ty France has had a monster season with the Padres. He's buoyed the lineup incredibly, batting .299 with 21 homers. France is usually batting cleanup for the Friars. Dustin Harris , on the other hand, has been a newer addition . Since joining San Diego (23 games), Harris has batted .338/.368/.437 and is now hitting second behind Fernando Tatis Jr. Both of them, along with others like breakout catcher Luis Campusano , Gavin Sheets and Samad Taylor , could be huge for the Padres offense this time around.

The other major problem for San Diego has been a lack of star power from their bigger names. Except Tatis, Xander Bogaerts , Manny Machado and Jackson Merrill struggled in the playoffs. The trio combined to go 23-for-107 (.215) between both 2024 and '25. Tatis, meanwhile, has gone a blistering 12-for-38 (.316). Though most of that came in 2024 when Tatis hit .423 with a 1.500 OPS across seven games.

That being said, the stars have been out lately for San Diego. Bogaerts is slashing .315/.393/.481 over his last 15 games. Despite a dip in his batting average, Machado is on the verge of his first 30-homer season since 2023. Merrill is batting .305 with 16 homers , and Tatis has hit 20 home runs since the All-Star break. If those four are clicking when the lights are brightest, the Padres won't need much else.

articles.title: Alabama Just Lost Two Defensive Playmakers Before South Carolina Game
articles.summary: Alabama will be without two key pieces of its defensive front when South Carolina comes to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday.The Crimson Tide’s first availabi...
articles.body:
Alabama will be without two key pieces of its defensive front when South Carolina comes to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday.

The Crimson Tide 's first availability report of the week revealed that edge rushers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu have both been ruled out for the Week 4 matchup.

That could force Alabama to lean more heavily on less-experienced edge players as the Crimson Tide prepares for another SEC test.

Alabama will be without Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu

Hill practiced Tuesday and was made available to the media afterward, but the sophomore is dealing with a lower-extremity injury. According to Yea Alabama , Hill is expected to miss a few weeks.

Hill has served as Alabama's backup Wolf linebacker behind Yhonzae Pierre , giving the Crimson Tide another option in its outside linebacker rotation.

Umeozulu's absence is particularly notable given the timing of the matchup. The senior transferred to Alabama from South Carolina and started against Florida State last Saturday, playing a season-high 31 defensive snaps, according to Pro Football Focus .

Umeozulu is dealing with turf toe, according to sources , and his return timeline remains undetermined. Alabama lists him as a co-starter at Bandit on its depth chart.

With both players unavailable, Alabama could turn to Jah-Marien Latham and Fatutoa Henry for additional depth on the edge.

The timing isn't ideal for the Crimson Tide. Alabama is coming off a 50-36 victory over Florida State in which the defense allowed 471 total yards, including 377 through the air.

At the same time, there is some positive injury news. Running backs Daniel Hill and EJ Crowell, along with wide receiver Noah Rogers and running back AK Dear, were not listed on the initial availability report.

Alabama enters the matchup ranked No. 8 nationally at 3-0, while South Carolina is 2-1. The Crimson Tide and Gamecocks are scheduled to kick off at 6 p.m. CT Saturday at Bryant-Denny Stadium on ESPN.

For Alabama, the biggest question now may be how the defensive front responds to losing two players who were expected to contribute to the edge rotation.

articles.title: Marlins prevent Cubs from clinching a playoff spot again with a 3-2 victory
articles.summary: Dansby Swanson drove in both runs for the Cubs, who needed a win or an Arizona loss to Colorado to secure an NL wild-card berth.
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — Kyle Stowers homered and the Miami Marlins prevented the Chicago Cubs from clinching a playoff berth for the second straight night with a 3-2 victory Wednesday.

Dansby Swanson drove in both runs for the Cubs, who needed a win or an Arizona loss to Colorado to secure an NL wild-card berth. The Diamondbacks beat the Rockies 5-3 .

Joe Mack's groundout brought home Augustin Ramirez with the go-ahead run in the seventh and the Marlins retired the next nine Chicago batters to win their second straight game after dropping three in San Diego .

Stowers hit his 21st homer, a two-run shot, off Kevin Gausman in the top of the sixth to break a scoreless tie. The Cubs evened things in the bottom of the inning when Swanson laced a broken-bat single into left field to bring home a pair of runs.

Cade Gibson (6-2), the second of four Miami relievers, struck out two in the seventh and Sandy Alcantara worked the ninth for his second save.

Reliever Ryan Rolison (9-2) took the loss.

Gausman struck out seven and allowed two runs, six hits and a walk in the first 5 2/3 innings. Miami's Ryan Gusto allowed six hits and two walks while striking out five in 5 1/3 innings.

Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong needed a stolen base to become the seventh player to join the 40-40 club but went 0 for 3 with a walk and remained at 45 home runs and 39 steals.

The Cubs have not named a starter for Thursday afternoon's home finale. RHP Tyler Phillips (5-6, 3.45 ERA) is scheduled to start for the Marlins.

articles.title: Mike Norvell Threatens Strict Action Against FSU Players Amid Growing Hot Seat Pressure: “Absolutely Unacceptable”
articles.summary: Florida State is 1-2 after two straight losses. Against Alabama, the Seminoles blew a 21-6 lead, gave up scores on nine straight possessions, and lost 50-36.
articles.body:
Florida State is 1-2 after two straight losses. Against Alabama, the Seminoles blew a 21-6 lead, gave up scores on nine straight possessions, and lost 50-36. Norvell had already seen the same execution issues. Now he is warning that players who keep repeating them could lose playing time.

"We lost both those games, and we did not play to the best of our ability," said Norvell . "And at the end of the day, I think that's my, if there's any part of that, then you will not see those players playing very long or much anymore, right? If we can't get up to go play our best football, that's not, that would be absolutely unacceptable. "

In an X post shared by Warchant, Norvell made his expectations clear as Florida State sits at 1-2 and 0-1 in ACC play. He still praised his players' fight after the Alabama loss, but his message going forward was firmer: repeated execution mistakes could start costing players their snaps.

"I thought we put ourselves in position but did not get the job done," Norvell said postgame. "But I am proud of the fight of our players. I mean, they're in the locker room. We all feel the disappointment, but also feel the urgency to get better… We lost to two good football teams early in the season, with ample opportunities to go and win it. We didn't make enough plays in either of those games to finish the job, and that's what we have to do."

Norvell is not putting all the blame on his players. After the Alabama loss, he said "none of it is solely on players" and admitted the coaching staff also has to put players in better positions to succeed. He pointed to missed signals, poor alignments, bad leverage and players being out of position, while also questioning whether the defense is being asked to do too much.

The numbers show why those issues are becoming difficult to ignore. FSU has surrendered more than 550 yards in back-to-back games, including 567 against Alabama. His staff is also under pressure to correct what keeps going wrong.

Central Arkansas now presents a very different test. Florida State returns home for a matchup it is expected to control against a Bears team making its first trip to Tallahassee. Central Arkansas still brings problems, particularly behind dual-threat quarterback Donovyn Omolo and a rushing attack averaging 6.2 yards per carry and 238.3 yards per game.

For Norvell, the significance goes beyond simply getting back in the win column. After two straight losses and recurring execution problems, another setback at home would bring even more attention to a program already searching for answers.

At Florida State, mediocrity is not the standard. The Seminoles have won national championships in 1993, 1999 and 2013, while Norvell raised expectations again with 10 wins in 2022 and a 13-1 season in 2023. Since then, FSU has fallen to 2-10 in 2024, 5-7 in 2025 and 1-2 to start 2026, leaving Norvell at 39-36 overall. For a program with that history, the bigger question is how quickly a championship-level run turned into another stretch of inconsistency.

The frustration around Norvell is already visible. Some fans have launched a website calling for his removal and have even discussed raising money toward his buyout.

Norvell's eight-year, $84 million extension runs through 2031, leaving Florida State facing a buyout of roughly $51 million if it moves on from him during or after the 2026 season. A loss to Central Arkansas would only intensify the questions surrounding Norvell's future in Tallahassee.

Next, Florida State gets Central Arkansas at home before hosting Virginia on October 3. After that, the schedule toughens quickly with road games at Louisville and Miami, followed by Clemson at home, giving Norvell little room for the same mistakes to continue.

articles.title: Did Graham Bensinger Cross a Line With His Mike Macdonald Interview Release
articles.summary: "In an era when every conversation can become content, there should be no gray area when it comes to what is and isn't on the record." The post Did Graham Be...
articles.body:
Graham Bensinger has interviewed some of the highest-profile people in sports and sports media. From Stephen A. Smith to Shaquille O'Neal, Bensinger's work offers rare, long-form interviews and behind-the-scenes looks at some of the biggest names in sports. His latest sit-down is getting plenty of attention, but not exactly for all the right reasons.

In his exclusive, nearly two-hour sit-down with Super Bowl-winning head coach Mike Macdonald, there was a portion of the conversation that didn't make the final edit for YouTube. However, it did make its way to social media, causing a firestorm of reaction online about the ethics of journalism. There are many ways to look at the moment. But mostly, it serves as a reminder that everything is on the record unless both sides agree otherwise.

While I've never worked in television, I have been in radio for nearly two decades. I've had the pleasure of spending time with thousands of personalities, talent and executives. Every time there's a conversation, I state when the recording has started and when it has ended.

It's not the law, but it's a courtesy. Informing the interview subject that everything said is now being recorded and is on the record unless otherwise stated establishes clear expectations. I've always honored that principle. Not because I learned it in school, but because I've learned through experience that it's always best to develop trust and relationships when you're as transparent as you hope the subject will be.

That's why those judging Bensinger's ethics based solely on the release of the clip are misguided.

In the clip , there's no indication that the conversation was being recorded. There's also no indication that it wasn't. There's also no disclaimer from either Macdonald or Bensinger indicating that the story he shared was off the record. In my short time working in television, one thing I do know is that once you sit in the chair, the cameras are rolling.

If the cameras are rolling, it's at the editor's discretion what gets included in the final product. If there are no disclaimers about what is on or off the record, the editor has a full canvas to paint.

According to reporting , the clip of Macdonald discussing his use of videos from Twitter was not included in the final YouTube product . That's the bigger question to be asked.

Not whether the content was meant for public consumption, but if it was important enough to post after the release of the full-length final product, why wasn't it included in the original interview?

The other question that needs to be asked is whether someone from the Seattle Seahawks' communications team was present in the room. If so, why didn't they speak up when the discussion was taking place?

If the interview with Bensinger was arranged solely through the head coach or his agent, then the Seahawks don't have much ground to stand on. They can't say the commentary wasn't meant for public consumption if no one representing the organization was present to establish that boundary.

The Seattle Seahawks likely won't grant Bensinger any additional access. Then again, does he need it? Probably not. But will other NFL teams and personnel follow suit? You can assume some will because of the attention this clip received.

Will it affect the guest roster Bensinger gets in other aspects of media and entertainment? It depends. His sit-downs are designed around storytelling and sharing the journey of the subject. Not everyone will shy away from Bensinger's digital following or the distribution he has with networks around the country.

You can also bet that Mike Macdonald will look inward at this situation as well. So will every athlete, coach and executive who sees what happened. Words have consequences. It doesn't matter if it's public or not.

Yes, off-the-record portions of conversations happen all the time. They will continue to happen every day. But unless something is explicitly stated to be off the record, everyone involved should assume the conversation is on the record. Especially in the setting Macdonald and Bensinger were in.

The lesson here isn't that everything said in an interview should automatically become content. It's that everyone involved needs to understand the rules before the first question is asked.

If something is off the record, say it. If something is not meant for public consumption, make that clear. And if you're the person being interviewed, don't assume a camera that's rolling suddenly stops recording because the conversation feels informal.

Trust is the foundation of any good interview. That trust doesn't come from assuming what the other person meant. It comes from establishing expectations, communicating clearly and respecting the boundaries that were agreed upon.

The Bensinger-Macdonald situation will eventually fade from the social media cycle. The larger lesson shouldn't. In an era when every conversation can become content, there should be no gray area when it comes to what is and isn't on the record.

If you want something to remain private, say so. Otherwise, once the microphones are on and the cameras are rolling, everyone should understand the rules.

articles.title: Chicago White Sox denied a chance to clinch a playoff berth, falling 5-4 to the Kansas City Royals
articles.summary: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Two results had to happen for the Chicago White Sox to qualify for the postseason on Wednesday. The Texas Rangers had to lose to the New Y...
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Two results had to happen for the Chicago White Sox to qualify for the postseason on Wednesday.

The Texas Rangers had to lose to the New York Mets . And the Sox had to defeat the Kansas City Royals .

The Mets did their part, but the Sox suffered a late 5-4 loss to the Royals in front of 17,114 at Kauffman Stadium.

The Royals went ahead in the seventh with an RBI double by Maikel Garcia , and then held on to deny the Sox the opportunity to clinch a postseason berth.

"It's baseball," catcher Kyle Teel said. "Come back ready to play tomorrow. Today's over with, how can we learn from it, be ready to win tomorrow."

The Sox also missed out on a chance to tie the Cleveland Guardians for first place in the American League Central. The Sox still trail the division-leading Guardians, who lost 1-0 to the Boston Red Sox , by one game. Both teams have four games remaining in the regular season.

The White Sox remain three games ahead of the Rangers for the final AL wild-card slot. The Rangers lost to the Mets 7-2.

The Sox fell in a deep hole early on Wednesday, trailing 4-0 after the first inning . Garcia drove in two with a single through the drawn-in infield. He scored on a double by Vinnie Pasquantino against opener Bryan Hudson . Pasquantino later scored when Colson Montgomery 's throw got past first baseman Munetaka Murakami on a grounder hit to shortstop by Michael Massey .

Hudson allowed four runs (three earned) on four hits in one-third of an inning.

"Just some ground balls that found the hole," manager Will Venable said. "(Hudson has) been so good for us. As far as our approach today with opening for (Erick) Fedde , that combination of (Hudson) to Fedde has been really effective for us, and today just didn't work out.

"Credit the Royals for putting the ball in play, finding the holes and we weren't able to stop them really that first inning."

The Sox rallied with four runs in the third inning . Teel drove in two with a single. Miguel Vargas had an RBI single and Murakami followed with an RBI double, tying the score.

"Just took White Sox baseball," Teel said of the team's response. "We just do what we do. We always fight, no matter what."

Fedde fought off the effects of a hard grounder to his right calf in the second inning to remain in the game. The right-hander allowed four hits, walked two and struck out two in 2 2/3 scoreless innings.

"It got the muscle of the calf pretty good," Fedde said. "X-rays were clean. Everything looks good. Just got to work through the muscle soreness and should be all right.

"It didn't feel great, but I felt like I was still able to compete at a pretty high level and, not the worst, but I think I could tell they didn't want to push me too far."

The score remained tied at 4 until the seventh when Garcia drove in Bobby Witt Jr. with a two-out double against reliever Hagen Smith .

"We talked about (setting up a lefty-lefty matchup by walking the right-handed hitting Garcia to get to Pasquantino)," Venable said. "It was just below the threshold as far as the gap between them that we typically do it.

"In hindsight, you wish that maybe you would. But the process was good. That's just one of those in which the threshold on that matchup was below what we typically do to walk somebody."

The Sox had one hit over the final three innings, a two-out single in the ninth by Braden Montgomery. Sam Antonacci lined out to center to end the game.

The Sox will have another opportunity in Thursday's series finale. A win, and they clinch.

"It's the goal when you come into the year to get a ticket into the playoffs and then anything can happen," Fedde said. "Being that close is exciting. It proves all the hard work these guys have put in. We look to earn that tomorrow."

articles.title: Thailand slams chaotic Asian Games organisation as 'musical chairs'
articles.summary: Thailand are the latest country to slam the organisation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, likening it to a "chaotic" game of "musical chairs"."It's...
articles.body:
Thailand are the latest country to slam the organisation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, likening it to a "chaotic" game of "musical chairs".

Athletes have complained of poor accommodation, long delays at airports and in boarding cruise ship housing.

Erratic transport services have seen competitors' buses to training and venues turning up late, or in some cases not at all.

The continent's biggest sporting showpiece, with more than 17,000 athletes and officials, has faced multiple issues during its first full week.

Some teams said there was a shortage of rooms and others complained about the quality of accommodation provided by organisers.

No traditional athletes' village has been built, as a cost-cutting measure, with participants instead staying in temporary container-style huts, hotels and the Costa Serena cruise ship moored in Nagoya port.

"It remains a problem, from the beginning until now," Chalitrat Chandrubeksa, deputy secretary general of the National Olympic Committee of Thailand, told AFP late on Wednesday.

"The number of (rooms available on) cruise ships and hotels does not match our actual number of athletes," he added.

"On the peak day, we required 201 beds on the cruise ship but they provided only 170.

"When athletes checked in and found their names missing from the list, they had to be placed somewhere else and when the new athletes arrived, the previous ones had to move out and look for other hotels.

Frustrated athletes have made their feelings known online, with complaints also about some of the food.

More than 4,000 people are staying on the ship in Nagoya's port and 2,000 in the cramped wooden container huts, called "villas" by the organisers without a hint of irony.

"We are solving the problem by finding replacement accommodations ourselves," said Chalitrat.

"We had to book our own and make advanced payments for food out of our pockets."

The shortages have meant the Thailand team having to put some staff far away from the games epicentre in the city of Nagoya.

"Our medical team has to stay about one hour 30 minutes from Nagoya.

"We had to rent additional vehicles from Tokyo so they could travel to look after the athletes.

"We just hope to fulfil and complete this mission as successfully as possible."

Games organisers said Thursday they were working constantly to improve services for athletes.

"We have already increased shuttle buses as much as possible to satisfy atheletes' needs," Asian Games organising committee spokesman Hiroshi Koshizuka told AFP on Thursday.

He admitted issues with transport had occurred but said "there had been no significant impact on the Games and no event has been delayed".

"We have set up a system to respond to complaints and we will address them in a sincere manner going forward."

articles.title: Monroe County Region high school sports roundup for Wednesday, Sept. 23
articles.summary: St. Mary Catholic Central fights off four match points to trip Flat Rock in a showdown for the Huron League volleyball lead.
articles.body:
St. Mary Catholic Central's volleyball team was facing a monstrous uphill battle in a showdown for first place in the Huron League on Wednesday, Sept. 23.

The Kestrels were down 24-20 in the fourth set after dropping two of the first three.

What did SMCC coach Kim Windham tell her players during a timeout?

"One point at a time," she said. "We had to keep our self-composure."

That's exactly what the Kestrels did, fighting back to win the fourth set, then coasting in the decisive fifth set for a 26-24, 15-25, 23-25, 26-24, 15-9 victory.

"It was a heck of a fight," Windham said.

The slight waver at the close of the fourth set was costly for Flat Rock in a match that was razor tight all night.

"We knew we were in for a challenge," said Flat Rock coach Morgan Delhey, who has most of the key players back from a team that was the state runner-up in Division 2 last season. "Kudos to SMCC, but we can't give up points like that at the end of the fourth set."

After pulling off the dramatic comeback in the fourth, SMCC took charge in the fifth.

The Kestrels raced out to 7-2 lead on twos kill and a tandem block with Alexa Turner by Avery Yeager and aces by Reese Foster and Avery Gramlich.

Claire Ryan racked up three kills, Allie Ruhlig added two and Turner served up an ace to help SMCC close it out.

SMCC suffered heavy graduation losses from a team that reached the state semifinals in Division 3 last season, but showed great poise throughout a night where neither team was able to get much breathing room.

The score was tied 10 times in the third set and 11 times in the fourth.

Reigning Monroe County Region Player of the Year Sarah Giroux had a huge match with 34 kills and 28 digs. Lily Klein also was a tower of strength with 22 kills, 29 digs and 4 blocks.

Zoe Ryan added 53 assists, 15 digs and 3 blocks for the 12-4-1 Rams.

Jaylyn Vanslambrouck, Jefferson : Rang up 14 kills and served 8 points in a 25-22, 25-21, 22-25, 25-19 victory over Grosse Ile. "We faced some adversity by dropping the third set, but were able to come back with a decisive win in the fourth," Jefferson coach Jason Stanke said. "We continue to learn and grow as a team."

Darby Philbeck, Airport : Directed the offense with 42 assists and served 3 aces to spark a 23-25, 26-24, 25-16, 21-25, 16-14 triumph over Riverview. Mya Stahr delivered a season-high of 18 kills to go along with 24 digs and 5 aces. Sophia Ruhlig (10 kills, 6 digs) and Katie Roecker (7 kills, 4 digs, 2 aces) also had strong performances and Myra VanWashenova, Jane Smart and Jenna Kemp led the defense.

Cristobal Zamarron, Flat Rock : Scored off an assist by Theo Meyer for the Rams' only goal in a 6-1 loss to Trenton. Collin Linder made 18 saves.

SHENZHEN, China (AP) — Anhelina Kalinina has given Ukraine a 1-0 lead in its Billie Jean King Cup tennis quarterfinal against Belgium with a 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-1 win Thursday over Jana Otzipka.

Seventh-ranked Elina Svitolina will try to clinch the quarterfinal for Ukraine when she plays 175th-ranked Greet Minnen in the following second singles.

The 474th-ranked Otzipka had 16 double faults.

Ukraine or Belgium will play the winner of Thursday's later fourth quarterfinal between two-time defending champion Italy and China in the semifinals, which is scheduled to be played Saturday. The final is scheduled for Sunday.

Earlier in the week, Spain advanced to the semis with a 2-1 win over Kazakhstan. On Friday, the Spaniards will face Czech Republic, which beat Britain 2-0 in their quarterfinal.

That left the Czechs on course for a 12th title in the competition previously called Fed Cup. The United States, which did not qualify for the finals, won a record 18 titles.

articles.title: A’s Beat Angels 7-3
articles.summary: Finished with the Angels for the year
articles.body:
The Athletics managed to finish off the Angels in convincing fashion on Wednesday evening. They beat their division rivals 7-3 to clinch their 63rd win of the year. That means no matter what happens over the final four games, the A's will avoid 100 losses this season. Plus, with tonight's win and the overall series sweep, the Athletics are looking extremely likely to finish ahead of the Angels in both the division and the league. We're not the worst!

Taking to the hill one last time for the 2026 season (and possibly his last time in an A's uniform), veteran Jeffrey Springs was looking to end his tough season on a high note. He's about to head to free agency so he came into this one looking to prove something to potential suitors this winter.

We got vintage Springs early on in this one. Through the first three frames he was in control, allowing just a pair of singles, one of which he picked off and the other he wiped out thanks to a double play. The lefty also collected a couple of punch outs. He was on early.

It wasn't until the fourth inning did Los Angeles finally start to connect on him. First it was future Hall of Famer Mike Trout launching a one-out solo home run, and he was immediately followed by another long ball, this one off the bat of Vaughn Grissom to make it back-to-back homers. Springs would get out of the frame and start the fifth but a one-out hit by pitch was enough for manager Mark Kotsay to come out and get his starter, ending his night and his season.

Jeffrey Springs: 4 1/3 IP, 5 H, 3 ER, 1 BB, 3 K, 2 HR, 84 pitches

That's it for Springs this season, and possibly in an Athletics uniform. He's made it known his pitching style isn't conducive to Sutter Health Park and with the A's in Sacramento for one more season his tenure with us is likely over. He'll end his season with a 6.18 ERA in 29 starts. Not great numbers heading into free agency but someone may look at his past results and think they can fix him next season. It just likely won't be the A's.

The bat meanwhile had a bit of a tall task before themselves tonight. The Angels were sending their top starting pitcher, rookie right-hander Walbert Urena , to the mound for tonight's series finale. Urena has faced the A's three times this season; two of his starts were gems, while his third and most recent was a disaster (7 ER). Which Urena would show up tonight against the A's?

It looked like the more recent one. The A's jumped all over the rookie in the first inning. Henry Bolte started things off with a leadoff single and quickly moved to second. That put him in scoring position for Lawrence Butler , who came through with a single of his own to drive in Bolte and give the A's the first lead of the night after just two batters:

Next up was Langeliers, but he grounded into a double play, seemingly ending the rally. With two outs Jeff McNeil worked a walk and Zack Gelof was plunked, suddenly putting two on for Donovan Walton . All the A's needed was a single for an extra run but he took advantage of a hanger from Urena, launching a massive three-run shot to make it 4-0 A's:

The inning would end but the A's offense wasn't done there. Shortstop Alika Williams led off the second with a single and stole second, setting up Bolte for an RBI opportunity of his own, one he would not waste:

That was Bolte's second hit of what would end up being a four-hit night for the rookie. He's now slashing .279/.362/.407 with 11 home runs and 21 stolen bases while playing solid center field defense as a rookie. What more could you want from him, A's fans?

Down 5-0 Los Angeles got those two home runs off Springs, then brought home the last batter that Springs faced around in the fifth to make it 5-3, with that run charged to Springs. This was suddenly a game again, and with at least four more innings to go. The A's could not let this one slip away, not after giving themselves a five-run head start.

Looking to put some distance back between the two teams the lineup got back to work. With Urena now out of the game the A's had to get a couple runs off the Angels' bullpen if they wanted some insurance. They got that when Langeliers connected on his 100th career double, a two-out, two-run base knock to make it 7-3 A's:

It's fantastic to see such a big part of the team hitting so well and not looking like he's missed a beat. Health is the most important thing, but he's now hitting .300 since his return. Still no long ball but the Houston series awaits!

While the A's have had bullpen issues all year long, those troubles did not rear their ugly head tonight. Righty Geoff Hartlieb took over for Springs and got five outs tonight. Fellow right-hander Luis Medina handled a clean seventh, lefty Hogan Harris had an uneventful ninth, and Elvis Alvarado finished things off with a 1-2-3 ninth.

Series sweep! Even if it is just a two-game set. The A's have clinched a non-100-loss season and are looking good for fourth place in the AL West. The offense did its job and then some against a tough opponent on the mound, and while Springs wasn't his sharpest he did enough for the A's and the bullpen to finish this one off.

The A's have just one series left before the offseason arrives. They'll welcome the division-rival Houston Astros to Sacramento for four games against the contenders, who have yet to officially punch their ticket to October. That means we'll be getting their best foot forward these next few games, possibly all the way through Sunday. Neither team has announced their starter for the series opener so stay tuned to find out the pitching matchup.

articles.title: El Renault 8 Gordini regresa del pasado… y podría tener futuro
articles.standfirst: El Renault 8 Gordini Concept pone a prueba los límites del diseño retrodeportivo aplicado a un modelo eléctrico, rindiendo homenaje a un pasado que bien podría convertirse en futuro.
articles.summary: El Renault 8 Gordini Concept pone a prueba los límites del diseño retrodeportivo aplicado a los vehículos de calle y, ahora con propulsión eléctrica, rinde homenaje a un pasado que bien podría convertirse en futuro.
articles.body: Desde 2011, Renault no ha preparado ninguna versión Gordini de sus vehículos de calle. Las dos últimas se basaron en el Clio y el Twingo, ese año y el anterior, respectivamente. Ahora presenta el 8 Gordini Concept para evaluar el impacto que podría tener entre una nueva generación de conductores que está convirtiendo al eléctrico Renault 5, de diseño retro, en un éxito de ventas. En 1946, el italiano Amedeo Gordini, nacionalizado francés como Amédée Gordini y apasionado por los motores, los chasis y los diseños más deportivos, fundó la marca que llevaba su nombre. Fue uno de los primeros preparadores de éxito en Europa y desde las décadas de 1930 y 1940 había trabajado en diversos proyectos, especialmente con Simca —en rallies—, una marca que por aquel entonces pertenecía a Fiat. A principios de la década de 1950, sus intereses empresariales comenzaron a divergir y Gordini dejó Simca para dedicarse por completo al entonces exclusivo mundo de la Fórmula 1. Esto ocurrió en 1951, pero en 1956 se vio obligado a abandonar el proyecto por falta de recursos financieros para competir con las poderosas Mercedes, Maserati y Ferrari. En la segunda mitad de la década de 1950 se multiplicaron los proyectos con Renault, tanto para coches de carretera como para rallies y circuitos. El programa de competición cobró impulso con la preparación de motores para las 24 Horas de Le Mans entre 1962 y 1966. Además, los modelos 8, 12 y 17 en los que trabajó y que llevaron su apellido alcanzaron una gran notoriedad en los rallies durante las décadas de 1960 y 1970. El 8 Gordini, que analizaremos en detalle más adelante, fue una especie de coche escuela para toda una generación de brillantes pilotos, entre ellos el legendario francés Jean Ragnotti. Durante este periodo de intensa colaboración se desarrolló el primer Renault-Gordini de carretera: el Dauphine Gordini, lanzado en 1957 y basado en el Dauphine convencional. El aumento de potencia fue bastante modesto —de 32 a 38 CV—, pero estéticamente el coche era más agresivo y buscaba acortar la distancia entre los circuitos y las carreteras. El 8 Gordini, una berlina lanzada en 1964, contaba con un motor de cuatro cilindros y 1.108 cc. La versión de serie tenía solo 50 CV, pero «el Hechicero» —como se conocía a Gordini por su habilidad para aumentar el rendimiento de los motores— casi duplicó su potencia máxima hasta alcanzar los 95 CV gracias a un sistema de alimentación con doble carburador. En una segunda fase, en 1966, aumentó la cilindrada hasta los 1.255 cc y la potencia, hasta los 110 CV. Este fue el segundo Gordini con mayor éxito comercial, después del Dauphine, y popularizó mundialmente el color Azul Francia —más tarde también conocido como Azul Gordini—, así como las dos franjas blancas que recorrían el frontal, el techo y la tapa del maletero. Se fabricó entre 1964 y 1970 y alcanzó un éxito comercial mayor que sus sucesores, los modelos 12 y 17, ambos de la década de 1970. Mientras tanto, Amédée Gordini ya había comenzado a retirarse del negocio. En 1968 vendió a Renault el 70% del capital de su empresa y se jubiló. En 1977, Renault terminó de adquirir Gordini, apenas dos años antes del fallecimiento de su fundador, en 1979. Paralelamente, se puso en marcha el programa para participar en el Mundial de Fórmula 1 con aquellos inolvidables monoplazas amarillos que introdujeron la tecnología turbo en la competición. Fueron tiempos complicados para la marca francesa, en los que los pilotos Jean-Pierre Jabouille y René Arnoux sufrieron graves problemas de fiabilidad que los obligaron a abandonar numerosas carreras, pese a conseguir buenas posiciones en la parrilla de salida e incluso liderar las primeras vueltas de algunos grandes premios. Por el momento, la marca francesa responde con un «quizás» cuando le preguntamos si este prototipo podría convertirse en un coche de producción. De ser así, probablemente tendría un mínimo de cuatro plazas, en lugar de las dos de este prototipo. Gran parte de su encanto reside en su diseño retro, una fórmula que suele tener una gran acogida en el mercado, como demostraron modelos como el Fiat 500 y, más recientemente, el Renault 5 E-Tech. En este caso, Renault manejó numerosas opciones. Tras convocar un concurso interno en sus centros de diseño, recibió alrededor de 300 propuestas. De ellas seleccionó dos, que posteriormente se reprodujeron a escala 2:5 —el 40% del tamaño real— para facilitar la elección del diseño ganador. Su longitud exterior es similar a la de un Clio: 4,12 metros. Sin embargo, es 11 centímetros más ancho —1,88 metros— y mucho más bajo que el actual superventas de Renault, ya que no supera los 1,27 metros, 18 centímetros menos que el Clio. Destaca la zaga vertical, de perfil inclinado, en la que se aprecia una parrilla que recorre toda la anchura de su parte superior. Es un claro guiño al diseño del modelo original, no una necesidad técnica, sobre todo porque los motores eléctricos requieren mucha menos refrigeración que los de combustión. Existen más conexiones con el estilo del Renault 8 de 1962, mucho más allá del color Azul Francia de la carrocería y de las dos franjas blancas paralelas que recorren longitudinalmente el coche de un extremo a otro. Empezando por el frontal, también muy vertical, con sus faros redondos, y siguiendo por la línea del parabrisas y el pilar trasero. Incluso se recuperan las estrías de la inscripción del número 8 que formaban parte del logotipo original, sin olvidar los pasos de rueda rectangulares del modelo lanzado hace 64 años. Pero parece menos probable que los motores eléctricos luzcan la famosa «G» que Gordini grababa en los propulsores en los que trabajaba. Las ruedas delanteras son de 19 pulgadas y las traseras, de 20, lo que contribuye a realzar la zaga del 8 Gordini Concept, de donde procede toda su potencia. No ha sido posible determinar si sus 270 CV se obtienen mediante uno o dos motores. Si emplea uno, estará situado en el eje trasero; si utiliza dos, se ubicarán junto a cada una de las ruedas de ese mismo eje, como sucede en el Alpine A390. Salvo por el sistema de apertura de las puertas, accionado mediante un gatillo eléctrico, todo en el habitáculo evoca el pasado. Empezando por los indicadores redondos, alineados horizontalmente en el salpicadero, donde destaca una moldura de aluminio cepillado que recorre toda su anchura. El mismo metal aparece en los distintos mandos del climatizador y en los botones de la transmisión situados en la consola central. Y, por suerte, no hay una pantalla táctil ocupando el centro del salpicadero. Tanto en la parte central de los asientos deportivos, con reposacabezas integrados, como en el propio salpicadero se emplean revestimientos de pana, otro guiño a las décadas de 1960 y 1970. Por su parte, los paneles de las puertas presentan costuras que evocan las franjas rojas de los pianos de los circuitos. El Renault 8 Gordini Concept se exhibirá a partir del 24 de septiembre en Le Défilé Renault, situado en pleno corazón de los Campos Elíseos. Se trata del emblemático espacio de la marca en la capital francesa y del establecimiento comercial más antiguo de una empresa en esta histórica y exclusiva avenida. Posteriormente, el prototipo se presentará ante un público más amplio en el Salón del Automóvil de París, que comienza el 12 de octubre. Serán dos escenarios en los que la acogida de los visitantes y, en el segundo caso, también de la prensa podría ayudar a determinar si estamos solamente ante un ejercicio de diseño o ante el anticipo del renacimiento de Gordini como submarca para las versiones más deportivas de Renault, ahora que Alpine ha comenzado a ampliar su gama de modelos.

articles.title: Bronze for Anant Jeet Naruka, Parinaaz Dhaliwal in Asian Games 2026 mixed skeet
articles.summary: Anant Jeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal added another medal to India’s shooting haul at the Asian Games 2026, winning bronze in the mixed skeet team
articles.body: Anant Jeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal added another medal to India’s shooting haul at the Asian Games 2026, winning bronze in the mixed skeet team event at the Aichi-Nagoya Games on Thursday.The Indian pair finished third in the final with 44 hits, behind China, who won gold with 52, and the Republic of Korea, who took silver with 51.India were locked on 44 with Korea after six series in the medal round. However, with the two teams tied, the qualification ranking came into play. Korea had entered the final in the higher qualifying position and therefore retained their place in the gold-medal contest, while India were eliminated and secured bronze. India's progression in the final was 7, 14, 21, 29, 36 and 44 across the six series.China eventually finished on 52 after seven series, with Korea ending on 51. India had completed six series at 44, while Qatar were eliminated earlier and finished fourth on 18.Naruka and Parinaaz had entered the medal round after finishing fourth in qualification with 138 points from 150 targets. Qatar had topped the qualification standings with 145, followed by South Korea on 143 and China on 140. The Indian pair had shot a series of 44, 47 and 47 to make the top four.Asian Games Full Coverage|Schedule|Medal TallyThe bronze also means both shooters leave the Asian Games with two medals each.Naruka had earlier helped India win bronze in the men’s skeet team event, alongside veteran Mairaj Ahmad Khan and Bhavtegh Singh Gill. Naruka had also finished fourth in the individual event.Parinaaz, meanwhile, was part of the Indian women’s skeet team that won bronze on Wednesday along with Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan. Their combined score of 331 gave India its first-ever Asian Games medal in the women’s skeet team event. China won gold while Kazakhstan took silver.The mixed skeet medal takes India’s skeet haul at Aichi-Nagoya to three medals, following the two team bronzes won on Wednesday.India have built on their two-medal haul from the 2022 Asian Games, where Anant Jeet Singh Naruka won silver in the individual event and was part of the men’s team that claimed bronze.The women’s skeet bronze in Aichi-Nagoya is also a landmark result, marking India’s first Asian Games medal in women’s skeet. articles.title: At 18, Salman Khan lost his father, drove taxi for months before becoming an Army man and now an Asian Games rowing medallist
articles.summary: For rower Salman Khan, winning an Asian Games medal is the latest chapter in a journey that began with family responsibilities, financial struggles and a
articles.body: For rower Salman Khan, winning an Asian Games medal is the latest chapter in a journey that began with family responsibilities, financial struggles and a job as a cab driver.The Indian rower won the bronze medal in the men's double sculls event alongside teammate Satnam Singh at the Asian Games 2026 on Thursday. The Indian pair stayed in second place until the 1,500m mark before slipping to third in the final 500m. They finished the race in 6:13.25 at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course.China's Yi Xudi and Yide Nie won gold with a timing of 6:09.37, while Uzbekistan's Pavel Sorin and Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov took silver in 6:10.49.For Salman, the medal has come after years of hard work and a life that could have taken a very different path.Salman lost his father at 18Salman was born in Pure Dhingai in Amethi district of Uttar Pradesh. His father, Mohammed Kasim Khan, worked in truck-body construction in Tauru, Haryana, where Salman completed his schooling.He was the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. When his father died of dengue, Salman was just 18 years old.With his younger siblings still studying, the responsibility of supporting the family fell on him. His dream of joining the Army had to take a backseat as earning a livelihood became his priority.Salman started driving an Uber cab in Delhi. He worked day and night to keep his family going.A friend's advice changed his lifeSalman had not given up completely on his Army dream. One day, while resting after a shift, a close friend reminded him that his height and physical build could help him in the Army. That advice pushed him to try again.He handed over the cab to another driver and spent four months preparing through hard running and training. He cleared the recruitment rally, medical and written examinations.In September 2018, he joined the Bombay Engineer Group (BEG), Kirkee, Pune.How Salman became a rowerAt the training centre, coaches noticed Salman's height and physique and introduced him to rowing. He knew nothing about the sport and initially had no interest in taking it up. With his family's financial situation, sport was not something he thought he could pursue.He refused several times. But the coaches continued to push him and eventually put him in a boat. They saw potential in him and began training him seriously.Salman's first inter-centre regatta gave him the first sign that he could make something out of rowing. He won a silver medal, which gave him confidence.The turning pointThe next major step came in 2021 when Salman cleared the ergometer benchmarks and was selected for the Army Rowing Node at CME Pune. Training alongside some of India's best rowers changed his outlook.What had started as a sport he did not even want to take up became something he wanted to pursue professionally.Salman began to believe that rowing could help him win medals for India.From national gold to international successSalman's progress continued over the next few years. At the 36th National Games in Gujarat in 2022, he won gold. At the 2023 Senior Nationals, he won gold in the single sculls against Olympian Dattu Bhokanal. That performance helped him earn a place in the India camp.In 2024, Salman won his first international gold at the Asian Rowing Cup in South Korea with Nitin Deol. That victory also earned him a promotion to Naib Subedar in the Indian Army.He followed it with a silver at the 2025 Australian Rowing Championships and another silver at the 2025 Asian Rowing Championships.Those performances helped him secure his place in India's Asian Games squad.From driving a cab to wearing the India jerseyFor Salman, representing India carries a special meaning because of where his journey started. He came from a village background and had to take responsibility for his family at a very young age.His mother, Jabrun Nisha, remained a major source of strength for him, while his wife, Sahiba Khatoon, supported him throughout his journey.His coaches and support staff also played a major role in keeping him on the rowing path, particularly during periods when he lost interest in the sport.At the Army Rowing Node, officers and coaches helped him regain his focus and develop as an athlete.Salman's journey from Amethi to the Indian Army, and from an unfamiliar boat to an Asian Games medal, has been built over years of perseverance, discipline and the support of his family, coaches and teammates.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: eSports star Yuki Kurihara, 11, aims to become youngest medallist
articles.summary: Primary school student Yuki Kurihara makes a flying start as he becomes the youngest athlete at this year's Asian Games.
articles.body:
Primary school student Yuki Kurihara made a flying start as he became the youngest athlete at this year's Asian Games.

The 11-year-old eSports star beat opponents almost three times his age in his native Japan on Thursday.

The youngster competes in Puyo Puyo Champions, a puzzle game similar to Tetris which was developed in Japan.

Players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them, creating chain reactions called 'dairensa'.

Kurihara beat all four opponents to top Group A and he will attempt to win gold on Saturday.

"The best feeling in the world is winning," Kurihara told the Japan Times. , external "When I lose, I cry and try not to think about it too much. When the play doesn't go well it's not fun, so I want to quit. But I always come back.

Japan's youngest athlete in Asian Games history could also become the competition's youngest ever medallist.

Indonesia's Bunga Nyimas holds the record, having won bronze in women's skateboarding aged 12 in 2018.

eSports has appeared in the previous two editions of the Asian Games, with Puyo Puyo being one of 11 medal events this year.

Kurihara says he eats eel to prepare for contests and secured his place on the Japan team at just 10 years old.

In February he beat an adult professional to win Sega's Puyo Puyo Grand Prix Final and he turned pro himself in April - two months before his 11th birthday.

The Asian Games are being held in Nagoya and the wider Aichi area from 19 September to 4 October.
