articles.title: WWE Raw Viewership Soars To Six-Month High For Roman Reigns Vs. Penta
articles.summary: WWE Raw scored its highest viewership since April for the highly anticipated world title match between Roman Reigns and Penta.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns and Penta made some magic on last week's episode of Monday Night Raw , in more ways than one.

On the Sept. 14 special edition of Raw from Mexico City, "The Tribal Chief' put his World Heavyweight Championship on the line against hometown hero Penta, and it paid off big time for WWE. According to Tudum (h/t Fightful ), "WWE Raw on September 14 drew 3.1 million global views on Netflix. The show ranked sixth globally and fourth in the United States. It's the most viewed episode since April for the Raw After Mania episode."

Reigns' highly anticipated match against Penta was his first world title defense on either Raw or SmackDown since June 2022, when he defeated Riddle to retain WWE Championship on an episode of SmackDown. Over the past several years, Roman Reigns matches in general have become increasingly rare. Non-PLE matches? Even rarer. Non-PLE title matches? Rare too.

The stars aligned, however, for Reigns to face the red hot Penta in Penta's home country, and with SmackDown's WWE Championship recently changing hands multiple times after brief reigns on SmackDown, there was an obvious air of excitement that Penta could follow in the footsteps of Sami Zayn and pull off a monumental upset.

With the buzz surrounding Penta's push and a rare Reigns match, Tudum (h/t Fightful) added that the Sept. 14 Raw featuring Reigns vs. Penta as the main attraction resulted in an additional 500,000 viewers from the previous week's Raw: "The September 7 episode scored 2.6 million global views. It ranked seventh globally and fifth in the United States."

According to date compiled by Wrestlenomics (h/t Wrestling Inc ), "Raw did not not hit the three million mark over the summer, with the highest global views for an episode coming on August 17 at 2.7 million."

What makes that number even more impressive is that Raw was going head-to-head with the season debut of the NFL's Monday Night Football on ESPN. According to ESPN , the Week One game between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos topped 23 million viewers, making it the most watched Week One edition of Monday Night Football since it moved to ESPN in 2006.

Reigns is widely considered to be one of WWE's biggest draws, having recently led the company to its biggest boom since the Attitude Era alongside top names like Cody Rhodes and CM Punk. Reigns' impact on Raw's Netflix viewership doesn't come as much of a surprise, but it does speak volumes for Penta, a newcomer to the main event scene in WWE.

Although there was some disappointment among fans that Penta did not pull off the upset over Reigns on Raw, WWE reportedly now views the high-flying luchador as a top star for the company. Just this past week on Raw, Penta was a last-second replacement for Solo Sikoa in a Money in the Bank qualifying match, and he went on to win it and earn a spot in the men's match at next month's PLE.

With the excitement surrounding Penta playing a key role in Raw's best viewership since April, that could bode well for the former AEW star, who now appears to be the leading candidate to win the coveted briefcase.

articles.title: Shakira Austin’s Most Improved Player case is about more than her scoring jump
articles.summary: One overlooked stat strengthens Shakira Austin’s WNBA award case
articles.body:
A bigger scoring average will get a player into the Most Improved Player discussion. What Shakira Austin has done for Washington deserves a closer look.

Austin entered the final days of the regular season averaging 17.0 points and 9.4 rebounds. According to the WNBA's awards analysis , her scoring was up 37.1% from last season and her rebounding was up 46.9%.

Those are substantial jumps for a Mystics team headed to the playoffs. The more interesting number is the one that moved in the opposite direction.

Austin is producing more with a smaller share of possessions

The league reported Austin's usage rate at 26.0%, down from 28.3% a year ago. Usage measures the share of a team's possessions a player finishes while on the floor. Austin has increased her production even as that share has fallen.

It is an important distinction in an award race that often rewards opportunity. A player can score more simply by playing longer and taking more shots. Austin is playing more, but the growth in her scoring and rebounding has outpaced her increase in minutes.

Her 19 double-doubles through games of Sept. 21 also ranked fourth in the league. She had totaled five across her first four WNBA seasons, according to the league's breakdown. That does not settle the award. Carla Leite , Marina Mabrey and other candidates have compelling arguments. It does show why Austin belongs near the center of the discussion instead of appearing as an afterthought on a list of scorers.

Washington needs the same version in October

The Mystics enter their last regular-season game with a playoff berth secure and seeding still in play. Austin's growth has given them an interior scorer and rebounder who can affect a game even when a possession is not designed to end with her shot.

That will matter in a best-of-three opening round. Defenses have time to target a leading guard. Rebounds, second chances and efficient touches near the basket offer another way to win.

The award voters will decide how much Austin improved. Washington will be more interested in whether her new level of play carries into the series beginning Sept. 27. If it does, this season's leap will have a more meaningful measure than a trophy.

articles.title: Chelsea have no January recall clause in deal for winger whose move already looks a disaster
articles.summary: There is no January recall clause in Alejandro Garnacho’s loan to Aston Villa – but that doesn’t preclude a return in the winter.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea co...
articles.body:
There is no January recall clause in Alejandro Garnacho 's loan to Aston Villa – but that doesn't preclude a return in the winter.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

As an Aston Villa fan who covers Chelsea professionally, there are few people better qualified to talk about the Alejandro Garnacho transfer than Matt Law.

The Telegraph journalist has today written a piece summing up the move, which has been a disaster so far. The Blues loaned Garnacho out for the season in a deal which contained "easily achievable" triggers to make it a permanent move.

But so far the winger has picked up just a handful of minutes, and didn't feature at all in any of Villa's last three games.

Garnacho could return to be loaned out again

Law reports that Chelsea and Villa do not have any January recall clause in Garnacho's deal, meaning both sides would have to agree to cut the move short. If he continues to be totally excluded, we can't see why either party would be against that.

The Blues have made it clear they want rid of the former Man U man, and the best way to do that is to get him playing regularly, putting him in the shop window. There are Spanish clubs said to be interested – but none of them will be able to pay very much for the Argentina international.

Links to a Man City defender from Chelsea are pretty interesting – but we will have to go a long way before we believe them.

articles.title: Wilson & Curtis leave Scotland squad to join U-21s
articles.summary: Forwards James Wilson and Findlay Curtis leave the Scotland Nations League squad in order to play for the Under-21 team against Azerbaijan on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Forwards James Wilson and Findlay Curtis have left the Scotland squad in order to play for the Under-21 team against Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

Hearts striker Wilson and Rangers winger Curtis had been training in Spain as part of the 27-strong group selected by new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli but will now miss the Nations League matches away to Slovenia and at home to Switzerland on Saturday and Tuesday.

The duo could return to the senior set up for for the 3 October trip to North Macedonia and the home game with Slovenia three days later.

The Under-21s are away to Bulgaria on the same day as the latter fixture.

Wilson, who has scored five Hearts goals this season, became Scotland's youngest men's international player at 18 years and 17 days old when he won the first of his two caps as a substitute against Greece in March 2025.

Curtis has made five Scotland appearances and is the nation's youngest World Cup player after late cameos against Haiti and Brazil in the USA this summer.

articles.title: What needs to happen for Jaguars defense to create more sacks?
articles.summary: The Jaguars have just three sacks through two games. How do they create more?
articles.body:
Through two games, the Jacksonville Jaguars' defense has generated just three sacks . Only six teams have generated fewer.

So what needs to happen to create more sack opportunities?

It starts with what happens on first and second downs.

"Keep them in second and long," Travon Walker said about creating more sacks, via Action Sports Jax. "You wanna get them in those obvious passing situations through where we can just pin our ears back and rush the passer."

Early down success for a defense puts the offense behind the sticks and in predictable passing situations. As Walker describes, it's in those instances that the defensive front can be more aggressive and get after the quarterback.

The good news for the Jaguars is that the run defense appears to be quite stout again, which will help keep opponents in longer down-and-distance situations. The pass defense, however, is surrendering a completion rate of 71.7% -- the fifth-highest mark in football.

That said, it's also on the pass rush to win their matchups as well.

Walker added that the Jaguars' defensive front is focused on the little things, like technique, hand placement, and where their eyes are.

articles.title: Cubs news: CM Punk led 7th inning stretch singalong during Chicago's loss to Marlins
articles.summary: It has been a busy week for Chicago native and Cubs superfan CM Punk, who threw the first pitch before the team’s loss to the Miami Marlins at Wrigley Field...
articles.body:
It has been a busy week for Chicago native and Cubs superfan CM Punk , who threw the first pitch before the team's loss to the Miami Marlins at Wrigley Field after guest starring on R.J. Decker .

He attended the game on Wednesday, Sep. 23, wearing Pete Crow-Armstrong 's jersey. Punk threw a decent pitch, and Clark the Cub embraced him afterward .

Later in the evening, he led the 7th inning stretch "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" singalong, working the crowd by saying, "All right, Cubs fans, I need you to get loud! Let me hear you!"

At the time of the 7th inning stretch, the Cubs had just gone down 3-2 to the Marlins, who scored a run at the top of the 7th to break the 2-2 tie. Unfortunately, Punk couldn't rally the Cubs to victory, as they failed to score in their remaining three innings.

Either way, it looked like he was having a blast. As for the Cubs, they dropped to 87-71 on the season and have lost both of their games to the Marlins in the series. They have a chance at redemption on Thursday, Sep. 24.

Why was WWE star CM Punk at the Cubs-Marlins game?

Punk, known as the "Second City Saint," was born and raised in Chicago , Illinois. He is known as a Chicago sports fan, especially of the Cubs.

His ties to the Windy City have remained an important part of his WWE persona. He has paid homage to the Flag of Chicago on his wrestling shorts over the years.

The "Best in the World" is coming off losing the Undisputed WWE Championship back to Sami Zayn during the Sep. 11 edition of Friday Night SmackDown. A couple of months earlier, on July 6, he beat Zayn to win the title in Chicago, making his surprise return after a two-month hiatus following WrestleMania 42.

articles.title: Colts’ Cam Bynum responds to 0-2 start and playoff concerns
articles.summary: Colts safety Cam Bynum explained why Indianapolis isn’t thinking about the playoff picture despite the historical difficulty of an 0-3 start.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts know what is at stake in Week 3, but safety Cam Bynum isn't looking beyond Sunday.

Indianapolis heads into its AFC South matchup with the Houston Texans at 0-2 following losses to the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs .

Bynum has recorded 16 tackles, including 12 solo, through Indianapolis' first two games.

Asked Wednesday whether the possibility of falling to 0-3 adds even more urgency, the six-year veteran made it clear the Colts aren't seeing the game that way.

"No, we don't think that far ahead at all," Bynum said, per The Athletic 's James Boyd . "When you show up on Sunday, you have to focus on that team right now, not focus on the playoff picture."

History explains why the question came up. Since 1990, only four of 165 teams that opened a season 0-3 went on to reach the playoffs, a 2.4% success rate, per The Sporting News .

The Colts will get an opportunity to change their trajectory at Lucas Oil Stadium against another 0-2 team.

The Texans also enter Sunday searching for their first victory, making the matchup a divisional test for both clubs, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: What Xander Schauffele claims he’s trying to get Jackson Koivun to do during Presidents Cup week
articles.summary: Xander Schauffele has suggested that it has been his mission to try and make Jackson Koivun laugh ahead of the Presidents Cup, with the youngster making his...
articles.body:
Xander Schauffele has suggested that it has been his mission to try and make Jackson Koivun laugh ahead of the Presidents Cup, with the youngster making his Team USA debut this week.

Koivun is the youngest player on Brandt Snedeker's team by some way.

The 21-year-old forced his way onto the side with an impressive run midway through the season, winning the 3M Open on his third professional start.

You can imagine that it is a difficult stage for Koivun to walk onto. He is now teammates with the likes of Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele , Justin Thomas, Collin Morikawa, and Wyndham Clark. Those five names have all won multiple major championships.

Xander Schauffele comments on how Jackson Koivun has settled into the Presidents Cup team

The American team has previously been accused of not being as close as their opponents over the years, particularly in the Ryder Cup. They have traditionally found it more challenging to come together after spending the majority of their season as individuals.

But Schauffele suggested that there is a good atmosphere within the team room ahead of the Presidents Cup , particularly with the rookies fitting in extremely well.

"It's been fun. We have a couple of new rookies on the team. They don't feel like rookies. They're obviously sort of battle tested. Our youngest rookie has already won on tour in his third start," he said.

"Nice to have those types of rookies playing versus I feel like when I was a rookie, I felt much greener, bluer, whatever the right term is. Our rookies feel like sneaky veterans. And they're fun. They're fun to play with. Good attitudes, and they seem to have no fear.

"The chemistry has been a lot of fun. A lot of laughing in the locker room. So I feel like my job is just try and get everyone as comfortable as possible as quickly as possible."

Jackson Koivun will be thrown straight into the deep end, with Brandt Snedeker sending him out alongside Justin Thomas in the opening session at Medinah on Thursday.

Schauffele commented on how Koivun has adapted to the environment.

"He's great. He's 21, you know. But he's been funny. Slowly opening up to us. He's second youngest guy to ever be on the team, which is pretty special," he said.

"Like I said, my goal is just try to get him to laugh, try and get him to open up, and then just get comfortable knowing that we all have his back and knowing that he'll have ours, too."

Xander Schauffele shares his admiration for Adam Scott ahead of his 12th Presidents Cup appearance

At the other end of the scale is Adam Scott . Koivun was not even alive when Scott made his first appearance in the event back in 2003. The Australian will be playing in the Presidents Cup for a 12th time this year.

Unfortunately, Scott is yet to be on the winning side in the event. And Schauffele spoke about how much a victory would probably mean to the 2013 Masters champion.

"I really like Adam Scott. No secret there. He doesn't want anyone's feelings on it. He's a competitor and he wants to get it done. He'll tell you that all he needs is one to make it feel really sweet, probably something along the lines of what he'd say," he said.

"So I love competing with him. We share the same physio week to week on a normal Tour schedule. So it's been nice to get to know him a little bit better. He's definitely inspiring to me. Aside from Presidents Cup. Just being that competitive at his age, at this time where golf is is really, really impressive. So nothing but respect for Adam."

With Scott no longer as prolific as he was once at finishing inside the top-10 at the majors, the Presidents Cup has arguably become even more significant in his career.

It would be a real shame if his playing days ended without him being on a victorious International Team. Of course, Schauffele will be hoping that his wait continues beyond this week at least.

articles.title: Why Colin Cowherd thinks Caleb Williams’ ’emotional’ injury reaction is actually a positive
articles.summary: The injury to Caleb Williams has been the biggest talking point across the entire NFL over the last few days. Chicago Bears fans were relieved to learn Willi...
articles.body:
The injury to Caleb Williams has been the biggest talking point across the entire NFL over the last few days.

Chicago Bears fans were relieved to learn Williams had only suffered a minor hamstring injury following initial fears of something much more serious.

There is even a possibility that Williams could play on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles .

Despite the positive news surrounding his injury woes, Williams has been roasted online for his emotional reaction as he was carted off the field at the weekend.

Although many have poked fun at the quarterback, Colin Cowherd is convinced this could be viewed as a positive for the Bears.

Colin Cowherd applauds Caleb Williams' emotional Chicago Bears reaction

A number of NFL players have defended Williams after suggesting the general public do not know how the quarterback was feeling at the time.

"My take, as somebody who now lives in a great city, Chicago, is that he is not just about the Bears. The league said, 'Okay, we're going to pick two quarterbacks to play on Thanksgiving and Christmas: Josh Allen and Caleb.' He is carrying the torch for the league, for Chicago, and for the Bears,' Cowherd said.

"And he's a kid. There is immense pressure on him. It's like being on Broadway and you lose your voice before the second show on opening night. It is emotionally devastating. So, regarding his reaction, I'm like, 'Guys, he's an emotional kid'."

"Caleb Williams is emotional but that is a good thing. It leads to some of his creativity, which leads to some of his brilliance as a playmaker on the field," Danny Parkins replied.

It is apparent that the Bears have high aspirations for their 2026 season, which may largely be why Williams was so emotional on Sunday.

A promising 2025 season has set Chicago up for a big year, but the Bears now have to pull themselves back to a winning record after their defeat against the Minnesota Vikings .

How quickly Ben Johnson will rush Williams back into action remains to be seen. However, the Bears do have a big game coming up on Monday against the Eagles.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard’s NBA contract extension with Raptors will look terrible in 2 years
articles.summary: The Raptors are going to regret the contract extension.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors are betting on Kawhi Leonard long-term to lead them back to the top of the NBA .

On Tuesday, the Raptors and Leonard reached an agreement on a two-year, $115 million extension that could keep him in Toronto through the 2028-29 season. Leonard is coming off one of his best seasons in recent memory, averaging 28 points in 65 games for the Clippers last season.

But the Raptors are making a massive commitment to an aging player with a long injury list, and this contract could look very different two years from now. The contract extension is going to look terrible in years to come, and here's why:

The Raptors aren't contenders in the East

Apr 5, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; LA Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard (2) before the game against the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images

Toronto improved this off-season by adding Leonard, but so did the rest of the Eastern Conference. Multiple teams in the Eastern Conference either jumped into contention or strengthened their already talented rosters.

The Knicks are coming off a championship, the Heat added Giannis Antetokounmpo , and the 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown . Cleveland also returns a core that reached the Eastern Conference Finals, while Detroit and Boston are both coming off 60-win seasons.

Toronto has Scottie Barnes , Kawhi, and a solid supporting cast, but that doesn't automatically put the Raptors in championship contention. If Leonard struggles to stay healthy, Toronto could find itself fighting for a spot in the play-in tournament.

This is where the contract could become a potential issue.

Leonard's extension doesn't begin until the 2027-28 season, when he'll be 36. He'll have aged even more and will be putting a massive hit on the salary cap, making it harder for them to acquire talent. This could be an issue, especially if Leonard begins to deal with injuries.

His contract extension will also make it harder to re-sign young talent and build around Scottie Barnes. The Raptors are taking a huge gamble on Leonard, hoping that his health and production will hold up.

That bet could pay off. If it doesn't, Toronto could be stuck with an expensive contract and limited flexibility just as the rest of the Eastern Conference gets better.

articles.title: Mark Messier ‘Horrified’ by Hiring of Former Red Wings Coach Mike Babcock
articles.summary: Mark Messier blasted the Oilers’ hiring of former Red Wings coach Mike Babcock, while Ray Ferraro offered a more measured view.
articles.body:
Mark Messier did not hide his reaction to the Edmonton Oilers hiring former Detroit Red Wings coach Mike Babcock.

During ESPN's NHL Opening Night media conference call, the Oilers legend voiced deep concern about the decision to bring Babcock back behind an NHL bench. As Greg Wyshynski highlighted on X , Messier's assessment was as sharp as it gets from one of the franchise's defining figures.

"I am absolutely shocked they hired him," Messier said . "I'm absolutely shocked from the stories that I heard from very good, reputable, character people about the way they were treated."

Messier then added, "I am just horrified about the whole thing, to be honest with you."

Babcock coached Detroit from 2005 through 2015 and led the Red Wings to the 2008 Stanley Cup. His coaching career has since been heavily scrutinized by former players, including in past controversy involving Johan Franzen .

Messier Also Questioned Edmonton's Hiring Process

Messier's criticism was not limited to Babcock himself. He also questioned Edmonton's reported process of having players involved in interviewing the coach.

The Hall of Famer argued that there must be a clear divide between management, coaches and players, warning that the structure can become complicated when players are closely involved in leadership decisions.

His comments renewed attention on Babcock's legacy in Detroit, where he delivered a championship but was later the subject of serious criticism from former Red Wings. Nicklas Lidstrom previously described Babcock as a demanding coach while discussing the allegations involving his former teammate .

Ray Ferraro Offered a More Measured Assessment

Ray Ferraro was also surprised by Edmonton's choice, but his analysis focused more on what Babcock will bring behind the bench.

"Nobody will have a question about what their role is or what they're supposed to do," Ferraro said . "Everything is extremely direct. It'll either work or it won't."

Ferraro noted that Babcock is organized, detailed and direct, while also acknowledging that few former players are publicly rushing to praise their experience with him.

That contrast frames Edmonton's gamble. Messier sees a troubling decision rooted in what he has heard about Babcock's treatment of players. Ferraro sees a coach whose structure and clarity could help the Oilers, while recognizing that the fit carries obvious risk.

articles.title: Why Daniil Medvedev Clears the Net Higher Than Anyone in the ATP Top 10
articles.summary: Forehand speed is easy to understand. Spin rate feels almost as straightforward. Put 82 mph and 3,177 rpm on a television graphic, and most viewers immediate...
articles.body:
Forehand speed is easy to understand. Spin rate feels almost as straightforward. Put 82 mph and 3,177 rpm on a television graphic, and most viewers immediately understand that the player has hit a fast, heavily spinning ball. The problem is that neither number tells you what actually happened to the shot.

The forehand data provided by Matthew Willis of The Racquet Substack , sourced from TDI, TennisViz, and Courtside Advantage, provides a much fuller picture. It tracks rally forehands over the last 52 weeks at ATP Tour events, excluding Grand Slams. It combines five measurements: where the player makes contact relative to the baseline, ball speed, topspin, net clearance, and eventual depth.

Once you place those numbers side by side, some assumptions about the best forehands in tennis become much harder to maintain. The most surprising example might be Daniil Medvedev . Medvedev owns one of the flattest forehands among the current Top 10, averaging only 2,453 rpm. Only Alex de Minaur produces less spin at 2,210 rpm.

Yet Medvedev's average forehand clears the net by 76 cm. Nobody else in the group clears it higher. That sounds contradictory until you include the rest of the shot.

Why Medvedev Clears the Net Higher Than Anyone in the Top 10

A Forehand is a Chain, Not a Speed Reading

Jannik Sinner sits at the opposite end of the spectrum. His average rally forehand travels at 82 mph, the fastest of the ten players, while also producing the most topspin at 3,177 rpm. He makes contact 1.03 metres behind the baseline and sends the ball only 67 cm over the net.

That is an extraordinarily aggressive combination. Sinner is hitting with enormous pace while generating enough rotation to help bring the ball back down. The International Tennis Federation's aerodynamic research explains the basic mechanism. Topspin creates a vertical aerodynamic force that pushes the ball down, so more rotation lets a player hit aggressively while still controlling the trajectory.

Carlos Alcaraz works in a broadly similar area. His forehand averages 80 mph with 3,113 rpm, but he makes contact significantly earlier than Sinner at only 0.77 metres behind the baseline. His average net clearance is 70 cm and the ball lands 3.90 metres short of the opposing baseline.

The comparison already demonstrates why looking purely at speed can be deceptive. Sinner hits two mph faster than Alcaraz and produces slightly more spin, yet Alcaraz typically makes contact 26 cm farther forward. Their forehands therefore begin from meaningfully different places on the court.

Felix Auger-Aliassime has the most interesting combination of aggression and penetration in the group. Auger-Aliassime averages 81 mph, second only to Sinner, with 3,048 rpm of topspin. He also takes the ball just 0.73 metres behind the baseline.

Despite carrying substantial spin, his forehand lands only 3.60 metres short of the opposite baseline, making it one of the deepest shots in the group. That combination matters. Taking the ball early already reduces the opponent's reaction time. Add 81 mph of pace and substantial topspin, and the pressure isn't captured simply by saying Auger-Aliassime owns the second-fastest forehand.

Taylor Fritz produces another distinct variation. Fritz averages 80 mph but creates less spin at 2,839 rpm. His 66 cm of net clearance is the lowest of anyone measured, while his typical ball lands 3.65 metres short of the baseline.

It is a much more direct flight. Compare that with Ben Shelton. Shelton's average pace is slightly lower at 78 mph, and his spin rate is similar at 2,888 rpm, yet he gives himself 75 cm of clearance over the net. Only Medvedev goes higher. Their speed and spin numbers do not look dramatically different. Their shot shapes do. That is precisely why isolated broadcast statistics can obscure as much as they reveal.

Medvedev makes contact farther behind the baseline than anybody else in the group. His average is 1.30 metres. Alexander Zverev is next at 1.25 meters, while no one else goes beyond 1.03. That means Medvedev's forehand generally has farther to travel before reaching the other side of the court.

He is also hitting it at only 75 mph, faster than just de Minaur among these ten players, and his 2,453 rpm is comfortably below the Top ten median. Put those numbers together, and one might expect a relatively harmless forehand landing short. It does not.

Medvedev's average shot lands 3.67 metres short of the baseline, making it deeper than the corresponding forehands of Sinner, Alcaraz, Zverev, Shelton, Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe. He does that while clearing the net by 76 cm. That is what makes the shape so unusual.

Medvedev gives the ball plenty of height but comparatively little rotation. With less topspin to create downward aerodynamic force, the ball is not pulled toward the court as aggressively as on the forehands of Sinner or Alcaraz.

The result is a shot that can travel a long way through the court despite relatively modest speed. That does not mean reduced spin automatically produces greater depth. Launch angle, contact height, incoming ball speed, shot direction and tactical situation all matter, and none is completely captured here.

It does demonstrate why describing Medvedev as simply a flat hitter misses much of what makes his forehand unusual. He hits flatter, yes. He also creates considerable margin over the net. The ball then keeps traveling.

Alex de Minaur offers an even stronger warning against judging forehands by speed. His average of 74 mph is the lowest in the dataset. His 2,210 rpm is also the lowest. Yet de Minaur produces the deepest average forehand of anybody shown, with the ball landing only 3.54 metres short of the baseline.

The first clue is his contact position. de Minaur makes contact only 0.70 metres behind the baseline, the closest of all ten players. He is therefore routinely taking time away from opponents before ball speed is even considered.

His forehand does not need Sinner's 82 mph when he is striking it 33 cm farther forward than Sinner on the average rally ball. It also carries relatively little spin, meaning it experiences less of the downward effect generated by heavy topspin.

The combination produces a very different type of pressure. Sinner overwhelms with velocity and rotation. de Minaur pressures with position and trajectory. Again, one number cannot tell that story. Zverev offers an interesting contrast. He hits considerably harder than de Minaur at 79 mph and produces 2,960 rpm, yet his average forehand lands 4.08 metres short of the baseline, one of the shortest figures in the group.

Cobolli is shorter still at 4.13 metres despite averaging 77 mph. Neither fact means their forehands are inferior. Depth itself is not a universal measure of quality. A heavy topspin ball landing four metres inside the baseline can jump aggressively off the court and push an opponent backward. A flatter shot landing much closer to the baseline can rush someone through reduced reaction time.

The quality of the shot depends on what the player is trying to achieve. That is the larger lesson from the data.

No Single Blueprint for an Elite Forehand

The ten players use remarkably different solutions to the same problem. Sinner combines the greatest pace with the greatest spin. Auger-Aliassime nearly matches that speed while taking the ball much earlier and finding considerably greater depth.

Alcaraz sits close to Sinner in both pace and rotation but makes contact farther forward. Fritz drives through the court with relatively little net clearance. Shelton creates substantially more height.

Medvedev stands far behind the baseline, hits relatively slowly and flatly, sends the ball higher over the net than anybody else, and still finds considerable depth. de Minaur takes the opposite positional approach, standing closest to the baseline and producing the slowest, flattest but deepest average forehand.

Even Tiafoe and Cobolli, whose raw speed and spin figures sit in the middle or lower half of the group, produce different outputs. Tiafoe averages 72 cm of clearance and 4.00 metres of depth, while Cobolli clears the net by 69 cm and lands 4.13 metres short.

No single combination defines an elite forehand. There are trade-offs.

More spin changes the ball's flight. More speed changes how much time the opponent has. Earlier contact takes time away before the shot has even crossed the net. Greater clearance creates margin but does not necessarily produce a shorter ball. Depth can pressure an opponent, although depth without sufficient pace or weight may not achieve much at all.

That is why speed rankings are useful but incomplete. The same applies to spin rankings. They describe what happened immediately after contact. Tennis continues after that.

Perhaps the most valuable thing about this data is that it explains why forehands that look completely different can all work at the highest level. Watching Sinner and Medvedev, nobody would confuse their technique or their preferred rally patterns.

The numbers explain some of the difference. Sinner's average rally forehand is seven mph faster and carries 724 rpm more topspin. Medvedev contacts the ball 27 cm farther behind the baseline, sends it nine cm higher over the net, and nevertheless lands it 29 cm deeper.

Those are not small differences, but they are fundamentally different solutions. The same is true of de Minaur. Nothing about seeing 74 mph and 2,210 rpm in isolation would suggest that his forehand should produce the greatest average depth in the group.

Then the contact position appears. Suddenly the picture changes. That is ultimately the problem with the statistics normally shown during matches. Speed and spin are interesting because they are simple. Tennis strokes are not.

A forehand begins with where the player is standing and how he meets the ball. Pace and rotation determine what happens immediately afterward. Trajectory takes it over the net. Aerodynamics alter the flight. Eventually the ball lands somewhere on the opposite side.

Only when you view those stages together does the shot really begin to make sense. And sometimes the player hitting the highest forehand over the net is the one everyone thought was hitting flat.

articles.title: Dolphins have made De'Von Achane look average. That's a shame | Habib
articles.summary: De'Von Achane's rushing average and average yards per touch are considerably down, which must concern the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS — This isn't a five-alarm fire. In a couple of weeks, it's possible we'll look back and say it was barely even a spark.

So let's call it a concern, one that can't become a trend.

The topic? De'Von Achane , the one playmaker the Miami Dolphins have who makes defensive coordinators perspire.

Achane entered this season as the 26th-best player in the league, according to the annual poll of peers.

Photos of Miami Dolphins-San Francisco 49ers NFL Week 2

Two games in, he has been just another running back, stuck behind 18 players with 110 rushing yards.

How much of that is on Achane? Not much.

Zoom out and you'll find an offensive line and a quarterback that haven't done enough to get proper mileage from the team's reigning MVP. As we've all seen the past few years, Achane burns teams with massive average gains whenever he runs or simply touches the ball.

After two games in 2024, Achane had 265 total yards from scrimmage.

Now look at his average gain per touch. It was 5.8 to start 2024, 6.8 last year … but is down to 4.2 this year.

This isn't the Achane who gashes teams, or at least looks like he's about to, every time. Remember, Achane entered the season with the second-highest rushing average by a running back in NFL history (minimum 500 attempts) at 5.6 yards, behind Marion Motley's 5.7.

De'Von Achane averaging 3.5 yards per rush

This season, Achane's rushing average is 3.5, a number that ought to make his linemen blush.

"We know we've got to be able to run the ball," Achane said. "So I feel like running the ball really is just a mindset."

Achane was held to 36 rushing yards in the opener but had 74 against the 49ers . He said his linemen entered Game 2 with "a chip on their shoulders. And they came out there and I feel like we got better."

Better isn't enough. Likewise, quarterback Malik Willis has found Achane for just 49 receiving yards. Put it together and only two teams are averaging fewer than Miami's 13 points per game. There have been occasions when Miami controlled the ball, but that's not enough.

"We've got to finish some of those drives," Achane said. "That's kind of the key thing this week. When we got in the red zone (against San Francisco ), I feel like we got penalties."

At 5-feet-9 and 195 pounds, Achane never will be confused with Derrick Henry . That puts the onus on the Dolphins to hit the sweet spot with Achane, giving him just enough touches to make a difference without grinding his legs into sawdust. And make no mistake, the onus is squarely on the coaches. Achane isn't about to demand the ball to coach Jeff Hafley.

"I've never been that type," he said. "Me and Haf, we always have a conversation. He always wants me, if I see something, to come up to him and tell him something. But I've never been that type of player to go up to somebody and tell them what to do or say — 'I need the ball more.' I've never been that type of player, so I'm not going to start now."

That's Achane looking out for the team. Now, the team must do more to look out for him. Which would benefit everybody.

articles.title: Justin Herbert fires back at criticism over lack of vocal leadership after Chargers’ 0-2 start
articles.summary: Los Angeles has scored 14 points in both losses to two of 2025's worst teams, and former teammates have debated Herbert's leadership since 2024.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert pushed back Wednesday on questions about the lack of vocal leadership, but an 0-2 start with a road trip to Buffalo up next puts pressure on him to back up those words with wins. The NFL spotlight will only grow brighter until this team shows up.

When asked a second time about the need for more vocal leadership, Herbert cut off the question. "I don't think there's a lack of vocal leadership at all," he said, per ESPN . "So, I'm going to stop you right there and say that it's very present."

Chargers offense stalls under OC Mike McDaniel

The Chargers lost both home games 26-14, first to the Arizona Cardinals and then to the Las Vegas Raiders . Las Vegas and Arizona held the first and third picks in this year's draft. Many wrongly assumed the Chargers would have an easy path to a 2-0 start.

The offense, now run by new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, has scored 14 points in each loss. Herbert threw two interceptions to Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses, but Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh blamed a bobble by tight end David Njoku on one and a wrong route by wide receiver Derius Davis on the other.

"I wouldn't change anything about Justin," Harbaugh said.

Herbert still showed his frustration Sunday. After a snap hit wide receiver Tre' Harris, he slammed his fists and yelled at teammates as he left the field.

Has Herbert's leadership been questioned before?

Former Chargers cornerback Chris Harris Jr., Herbert's teammate in 2020 and 2021, questioned him in June 2024. "He's missing that clutch factor, like a Mahomes ," Harris said, per Sports Illustrated .

Left tackle Rashawn Slater defended Herbert the next month. "It's funny, everyone who calls Justin a quiet leader isn't actually on the team, so they have no idea what his leadership is like," Slater said .

Offensive lineman Trey Pipkins echoed him last season. "I feel like it's been talked about that he's not very vocal, but he's always been very vocal when he's with us," Pipkins said .

Still, the doubts grew after a 16-3 wild-card loss at New England on Jan. 11 dropped Herbert to 0-3 in the playoffs. When asked if he could still win a playoff game, the former Oregon star answered, "I don't know," and added , "I haven't figured it out yet, and it hasn't happened."

Herbert faces Bills, Seahawks and Chiefs

Herbert's teammates have vouched for him for years, but a quarterback with no playoff wins needs to show that leadership on Sundays instead of defending it on Wednesdays. The outburst against Las Vegas showed the fire Slater described, and Herbert should aim it at the six fumbles that hurt the offense against the Raiders.

The Chargers' upcoming schedule isn't pulling any punches for the struggling franchise. Los Angeles plays at Buffalo on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET, then visits the Seattle Seahawks, hosts the Denver Broncos and visits the Kansas City Chiefs before its bye. A win over the Bills, while everyone watches to see how the Chargers respond to a slow start, would give Herbert the clearest proof that his teammates are following his lead.

articles.title: India’s surfers look to make waves at the 2026 Asian Games
articles.summary: Indian surfers overcame huge challenges to reach the Asian Games and now dream of competing at the 2028 Olympics.
articles.body:
Kovalam and Mumbai, India – When Sugar Shanti Banarse and Kamali Moorthy entered their first surfing event in 2022, the girls could scarcely have imagined they would end up representing India at the Asian Games within a few years.

Though the competition at the Covelong Classic in Kovalam, about an hour’s drive from Chennai in Tamil Nadu, southern India, featured just seven women among about 50 competitors, the possibility of winning was an afterthought. Their intention was to simply get a taste of competition.

At 12, Moorthy was the youngest of the lot, thrilled to surf alongside some of the senior girls. She failed to catch a single wave, but the experience stayed with her. She vowed to train harder and return stronger.

Finishing second was a decisive moment for Banarse, then aged 16. A recreational surfer until then, she loved the competitive aspect of the sport. In that moment, she knew she wanted to be a professional.

The duo has come a long way since then. Alongside their male counterparts Kishore Kumar and Sivaraj Babu, they will take on the best continental talent at September’s Asian Games in Japan, where surfing makes its debut and runs from Friday until Tuesday.

“We’ve been putting in the work over the last couple of years and made good progress. It’s our time to shine now,” Banarse told Al Jazeera.

Even though India has thousands of miles of coastline and breaks of different kinds, it’s taken a while for surfing to catch on.

India’s team coach Samai Reboul comes from the first generation of Indian surfers, who had few resources at their disposal. He would watch holidaymakers surf near his home in Auroville, Tamil Nadu in the late 1990s and had a go when they lent him a board. He was soon hooked.

“I grew up at a time when there were no coaches, no access to training material and no surfboards. [It was] really frustrating,” he told Al Jazeera.

Surf schools started cropping up along the coast over the next few years. This is how Banarse, now 20, got her first opportunity back home in Mandrem in Goa, when she decided to accompany a friend. Moorthy, now 16, was luckier – her uncle is a surf instructor who gave her the first lesson off the coast of Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu.

Kumar, 18, and Babu, 22, hail from families who fish for a living in Kovalam and Mahabalipuram, respectively. They started out by jumping into the sea on hot summer days, then body surfing, before finally hopping onto a board.

“A local school in Mahabalipuram would let us use surfboards in exchange for chores. There were a few boards and many boys, so a lot of fights once the patience ran thin,” Babu told Al Jazeera.

Though their lives revolved around the sea, it was difficult to get their families to understand what they were chasing.

A beating awaited Kumar when his family discovered he was sneaking away to surf – they considered it a waste of his time.

Babu was expected to help his father with his fishing, as his elder brother had done.

Moorthy’s mother, who runs a beach shack, knew what the harsh sun could do to her daughter’s complexion and asked her to stay out of the water.

“She was worried I would get [too dark], but at the back of her mind, she knew I was enjoying surfing and that it would reach a point of no return. And here I am today,” Moorthy says, laughing.

More importantly, the sport lacked structure. Though the Surfing Federation of India (SFI) was launched in 2011, there were no regular competitions, and participants had to fend for themselves when it came to travel and accommodation. Babu doubled up as an instructor and banked on community support to make money to compete. He once had to camp in a forest during an event in Mangaluru.

“My family didn’t quite understand the scope of what I was doing. But I had some imagination of what I wanted to achieve and persisted against their wishes,” Babu says.

Circumstances improved after Arun Vasu took over as the president of the SFI in 2020. As chairman and managing director of the prominent Indian conglomerate TT Group, he secured money from the company’s Corporate Social Responsibility funds to support a handful of athletes. The older surfers were encouraged to pursue their coaching and judging licences to improve the level of domestic competitions.

Meanwhile, Vasu worked towards getting the SFI recognised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. That moment arrived in March 2025, and changed the trajectory of the sport. Besides the injection of funds through the government-run Sports Authority of India, it brought stability for the SFI. Its members could now focus all their energy on growing the sport.

“The first generation of Indian surfers worked really hard without much support. They’ve brought us to this point where we are enjoying the benefits,” Moorthy says.

The goal was to prepare the athletes for the Asian Games. Reboul started monitoring the team and refining their technique during camps. A sports psychologist worked on the mental aspect of competition, while other staff focused on improving physical conditioning.

“Besides quality equipment, what really changed was access to cameras and software for video analysis. Even outside of camp, they could send across videos through which I could offer feedback,” Reboul said.

Over the last few years, the SFI has hosted prestigious competitions such as the World Surf League series and the Asian Surfing Championships, which have allowed Indians to rub shoulders with top international surfers. Trips across Asia have given them a feel for different conditions as well as elite competitions.

“It’s very different from a few years ago when we had limited opportunities to train systematically,” Banarse says.

Their performances have shown promise. Ramesh Budihal took bronze at the Asian Surfing Championships in August 2025, and a few months later, Kumar won silver at the Asian ProAm Surf Series.

“At the Asian Championships last year, [Kumar] beat Ikko Watanabe of Japan, a country that is up there [with the best]. So we know it’s possible [to compete],” Reboul says.

The focus is also on developing the next generation of surfers. SFI has joined the Asian Surf Ecosystem’s Grom Patrol – youth surf training camps and competitions – and runs three age group contests (under-12s, under-14s and under-16s), with the winners qualifying for the final in Bali.

Besides the talent that usually comes from fishing communities along the coast, it has attracted young surfers from cities such as Chennai, Bengaluru and Mumbai. And more importantly, girls who are ready to test the waters.

“We’ve struggled to find women surfers, so it was really encouraging to see 15-odd girls in every competition,” Vasu says. “Parents see a future, and these kids are hungry to learn. It makes us realise we are doing something right.”

Indian surfers still face a number of challenges. The monsoon season means surfers need to constantly shuttle between the two coasts or travel abroad to train year-round, which requires resources. There is also a need to create a deeper pool of skilled coaches to work with young athletes.

“More of the older surfers are getting into training. This year, we brought down an experienced coach, Ivan Villalba, to conduct a programme for them,” Reboul said.

“Good training and a competitive surf culture is what is required to put India on the map, rather than get a particular athlete to win.”

In the world of Asian surfing, India is still a young nation compared to the likes of Indonesia and Japan. Competing at the Asian Games will be valuable exposure for the current crop, especially ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

“A lot has happened for Indian surfing in the recent past. Some of the guys I’ll be competing against are my idols and I know I can put up a good fight for the podium,” Kumar says.

“The dream is to represent India at the Olympics.”

articles.title: 2 more Arsenal players called up late by England youth teams
articles.summary: Two Arsenal youngsters have received late England youth call-ups, with the first youth internationals of the break kicking off on Wednesday.Photo via Ranson...
articles.body:
Two Arsenal youngsters have received late England youth call-ups, with the first youth internationals of the break kicking off on Wednesday.

Arsenal's list of England youth call-ups has received yet another update, with Khari Ranson and Andre Harriman-Annous both added to the England u20 squad.

England have confirmed that Ranson and Harriman-Annous will replace Finlay Herrick and Jimmy-Jay Morgan respectively, with the West Ham and West Brom youngsters both picking up injuries.

Arsenal had initially had eight players called up for England youth duty, but that number was reduced to seven after Marli Salmon was forced to pull out due to injury.

Yet with Ranson and Harriman-Annous now involved, the total is back up to nine.

The first of Arsenal's England youngsters was in action on Wednesday, with Charlie Phillips playing for the u17s against the Republic of Ireland .

It was generally a very good game for England, who thrashed their friendly opponents 5-1. Phillips will just be disappointed to have conceded a curling effort in the 90th minute to deny him a clean sheet.

Arsenal duo Mylo Bernard and Vincent Joseph were called up by the England u17s as well, but neither of them were involved in the Ireland match. With a 28-player squad, it's likely there will be significant rotation between fixtures.

articles.title: 'Honoured' Reedijk attracted by Hibs' ambition
articles.summary: Dutchman Marink Reedijk is "honoured" to become Hibs boss and insists the club's ambition was a driving force in his decision to join.  The 35-year-old moves...
articles.body:
Dutchman Marink Reedijk is "honoured" to become Hibs boss and insists the club's ambition was a driving force in his decision to join.

The 35-year-old moves to Leith after leading Beveren - where he forged a reputation for attacking football - to the Belgian top flight before stepping down in the summer.

Reedijk previously held academy roles at Ajax and West Brom plus senior coaching positions at KSV Roeselare, Vitesse and RSCA Futures.

"I am honoured to be appointed manager of Hibernian Football Club," he said.

"This is one of the biggest clubs in Scottish football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

"I can feel the ambition and see the clarity of what the club is trying to achieve. That was a big part of what attracted me here.

"I want us to be an assertive team - brave, intense and committed. A team that gives everything, plays with purpose and gives our supporters something to really get behind.

"There is quality and potential in the squad, and good work has already been done. My first job is to get to know the players, build on those foundations and make sure we are ready for Dundee United."

articles.title: Former ASU RB Raleek Brown making most of his time as a Longhorn
articles.summary: Raleek Brown has not disappointed as a Longhorn. The former Arizona State Sun Devils running back is making the most of his opportunities at Texas.
articles.body:
Over the offseason, the Texas Longhorns completely reshaped their running back room. Their additions included Hollywood Smoothers and Raleek Brown, both coming off career years at other programs. While Smoothers has taken on the lead role, Brown has made the most of his opportunities and been a welcome addition to a team chasing a national title.

Through his first three games as a Longhorn, Brown has recorded 129 yards on 31 carries. The California native has also found the end zone twice while averaging 4.2 yards per carry. While the season is far from over, Brown only needs two more rushing touchdowns to match his career high.

As Brown has made an impact with his legs, he has also contributed in the passing game. He has hauled in seven receptions for 22 yards and helped make Arch Manning's life easier. That has been a welcome sign for Texas, as it has allowed them to use Brown in various ways. If Brown stays healthy, that should continue.

Although Brown's Longhorn career is just getting started, he is showing that his 2025 campaign was no fluke. In his final season as a Sun Devil, the Longhorns ' newest weapon set career highs in rushing yards with 1,141 and rushing touchdowns with four. It also marked the first time that Brown had over 100 carries in a season. That is partly why Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian made Brown a priority when he entered the portal.

With SEC play on the horizon, Brown will continue to be an important piece. As long as he hangs onto the football and continues to frustrate defensive coordinators, Brown could have a memorable run in the burnt orange.

articles.body:
Napoli have confirmed that midfielder Scott McTominay is back with the club and that he began his recovery work in the gym in Naples on Thursday following a recent procedure on his heart.

McTominay back in the gym with Napoli after heart procedure

McTominay has missed Napoli's last four matches across all competitions after having a minor procedure carried out on his heart to fix a mild, benign arrhythmia earlier this month.

NAPLES, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Scott McTominay of Napoli is challenged by Lucas Da Cunha of Como during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Como 1907 at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on August 30, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)

It is understood that McTominay and the club took the decision to have the procedure in September in order to minimise the number of matches that the midfielder would miss, given that there is an extra-long international break between the end of September and early October .

The procedure was carried out in the player's hometown of Manchester on September 8, and the club confirmed that he would require a rest period of around two weeks.

Napoli have now confirmed in a statement that McTominay is back in Naples and that he began carrying out individualised work in the gym on Thursday.

The Scotland international, not available to Sebastien Pocognoli during the international break, will be aiming to return to competitive action in time for Napoli's next Serie A match at home against Frosinone on October 10. They will be in Champions League action away against Villarreal the following Tuesday, October 13.

articles.body:
Chairman Ian Gordon has vowed to financially back new Hibs manager Marink Reedijk, who emerged as the "standout candidate" in the club's search.

"He impressed everyone involved in the process with his clarity, intelligence and drive," said Gordon.

"He shares our ambition to develop players and consistently compete at the top end of Scottish football and in Europe.

"Marink has our backing and we will continue to invest in the team to give him the best possible platform to succeed.

"We're delighted to welcome Marink and his family to the club."

Sporting director Malky Mackay described the 35-year-old former Beveren head coach as an "excellent fit to take the team forward".

"His teams are proactive, high energy and dynamic. What also stands out is his ability to develop individuals and create a strong collective environment," Mackay added.
